bullets: How energy flows one way through food chains and webs, why only about 10% moves up each trophic level, and how carbon cycles while habitats must be protected
slides.heading: JC H2 biology — ecology: energy flow and the carbon cycle
slides.notes: Welcome everyone in and say: today we trace energy and carbon through ecosystems - food chains and webs, the pyramid of energy, the carbon cycle, conservation, and the trap that energy is recycled.

bullets: Read food chains and food webs, explaining that arrows show energy flow from food to feeder
Explain the pyramid of energy and why only about 10% of energy moves up each trophic level
Describe the carbon cycle and conservation, and correct the claim that energy is recycled
slides.heading: What we will learn
slides.notes: Read the three goals aloud and tell the class: keep these in mind, because the exit ticket at the end will ask you to do exactly these things, including correcting the energy-recycling trap.

bullets: A rabbit eats grass, a fox eats the rabbit, and decomposers break down the dead
Does the energy in the grass come back round to the grass again, or does it leave for good?
slides.heading: If energy kept looping round, would food chains ever run out?
slides.notes: Ask the class to commit to a guess before any definitions: loops round forever, or flows one way and leaves as heat? Take two or three answers, then say: hold them, because scene s6 settles this exactly.

bullets: Energy enters as sunlight, moves from food to feeder along arrows, and leaves as heat - it is never recycled
Matter is different: carbon, nitrogen and water cycle between air, living organisms and decomposers
slides.heading: One idea, six scenes: energy flows one way, matter cycles
slides.notes: Say this slowly, because it is the big idea: energy flow is one-way and matter cycling is a loop, and confusing the two is the trap this whole lesson is built to correct.

bullets: A food chain is a sequence of trophic levels: producer, then primary consumer, then secondary consumer
Arrows point from food to feeder - grass to rabbit to fox - because they show the direction of energy flow
slides.heading: Food chains: arrows follow energy flow
slides.notes: Follow the red energy dot: it enters the grass, then moves with each feeding step. Say: arrows follow energy, so they point from the organism being eaten to the eater.

bullets: Real communities are webs, not single chains: grass feeds both rabbit and mouse, and mouse is eaten by both fox and owl
Because pathways interlink, removing one species sends ripples through the whole web
slides.heading: Food webs: one dot splits into two
slides.notes: Watch one energy dot split into two pathways through the web. Say: a web shows every feeding link at once, so a change to one species reaches them all.

bullets: Only about 10% of the energy at one trophic level becomes the next level; the rest is lost as heat, in waste and in life processes
That steep loss is why pyramids of energy narrow so fast and why food chains stay short
slides.heading: Pyramid of energy: only 10% moves up
slides.notes: Watch the energy dot shrink as it climbs the pyramid. Say: each level keeps only a tenth, so there is never enough energy left to support many levels above.

bullets: Photosynthesis draws carbon dioxide from the air into green plants, fixing carbon into food
Respiration and combustion return carbon dioxide to the air, and decomposers release carbon from dead matter - while burning fossil fuels releases ancient carbon all at once
slides.heading: The carbon cycle: one dot, round and round
slides.notes: Follow the blue carbon dot round the full loop and contrast it with energy: carbon really does cycle, travelling from air to plants and back to air again.

bullets: Habitat loss and fragmentation shrink populations: small isolated fragments cannot hold species that need large territories
Protected corridors reconnect fragments, letting individuals and genes move between them again
slides.heading: Conservation: when habitat shrinks, species vanish
slides.notes: Watch each patch shrink under pressure and its species label vanish with it. Say: the fastest way to lose species is to lose their habitat, and corridors fight back by reconnecting the fragments.

bullets: The trap claim in full: Energy is recycled through the ecosystem. It feels true because matter cycles - but the evidence in this scene says otherwise
Energy flows one way - sunlight in, heat out: what is recycled is matter - carbon, nitrogen and water.
slides.heading: A common mistake: energy is not recycled
slides.notes: Name the trap out loud: Energy is recycled through the ecosystem. Then land the correction: Energy flows one way - sunlight in, heat out: what is recycled is matter - carbon, nitrogen and water.

bullets: If producers hold 10 000 kJ of energy, only about 1 000 kJ reaches primary consumers and about 100 kJ reaches secondary consumers
Work it level by level: multiply by a tenth at each trophic step, just as the shrinking dot shows in scene s3
slides.heading: Worked example: the 10% energy payoff
slides.notes: Talk through the numbers level by level as in scene s3, then state the rule from the scene: about 10% moves up, so each level keeps only a tenth of the energy below it.

bullets: Draw the food chain grass -> rabbit -> fox with arrows in the energy-flow direction, then estimate how much of 10 000 kJ at the producers reaches the fox
Careful - a classmate says: Energy is recycled through the ecosystem. Correct them in one sentence, naming what is actually recycled
slides.heading: Your turn: trace the flow, then judge the claim
slides.notes: Give pairs three minutes, then cold-call one pair on each part: press them on the arrow direction and the 10% estimate first, then on the exact sentence they used to correct the claim: Energy is recycled through the ecosystem.

bullets: On your own: explain why food chains stay short, using the pyramid of energy and the 10% rule
Watch out for the trap one last time: Energy is recycled through the ecosystem. Say how energy really moves, and name what is recycled instead
slides.heading: Exit ticket: show what you know
slides.notes: Collect these before anyone leaves and say: I am looking for the 10% rule in your first answer, plus one clear one-way energy sentence in your second. Anyone repeating the claim Energy is recycled through the ecosystem. needs the trap scene again.
